name: Fran Drescher
summary: Drescher is a Democratic-aligned actress who led SAG-AFTRA through the 2023 strike, framing it as workers against greedy studio executives, and has campaigned on women's cancer awareness and removing carcinogens from consumer products. She has called herself anti-capitalist and favors regulation of industry and AI, and has opposed COVID vaccine mandates. Her recorded positions on most political questions are few.

Merged with an independent claude-haiku-5-5 audit: 3 answers taken from it, 2 agreed, 0 conflicts settled by the integrator.

claude-haiku-5-5 notes: Only statements she made about labor, the studios, capitalism and AI were found in the sources opened. The Hollywood Reporter and Backstage interviews, the Rolling Stone AI article and the Vulture original could not be opened (paywall, 402/403), and web search was unavailable late in the audit, so coverage is thin. Her 2023 comments on AI are mainly about protections and regulation, which no statement asks about directly, so they are left null. Health and environment advocacy (Cancer Schmancer, chemicals in consumer products) was found only in secondary reports without her words on government action, and is null.

Later pass (claude-sonnet-5-5, 2026-11-20): added her 2015 City & State interview, her 2022 remarks on abortion bans and The Nation's 2023 profile; searched the MediaSum CNN/NPR corpus (her own turns are mostly on cancer advocacy and The Nanny), her 2005 Senate testimony on gynecologic cancer (medical diagnosis and insurers; no statement matches), the 2023 Sanders livestream, and searches on guns, Israel, immigration, healthcare and climate (only second-hand characterisations or nothing). Officiating a 2012 same-sex wedding is an event, not a stated position, so same-sex marriage stays null. The uncertainty rule still fails: the public record is too thin for most dividing lines.
